1_blockout.notes: SCULPT REFERENCE ONLY - never shipped, never copied to assets/models/, never rigged. TRELLIS.2 (Pixal3D pruned) on the approved front, birefnet cut-out verified (full arm span and fingertips kept), 3 seeds (101/202/303) at the user's character settings (700k faces, 4096 px). s202 picked for its faceted gauntlet plates, head/beard and colour blocking; known defects (thin fingers, no lava-crack geometry or emissives, soft face, detached lower-leg shells under the skirt, fused cloth, baked lighting) are listed in reports/blockout_report.md section 6. 2_production_mesh.notes: Production mesh made by the AI pipeline, not a stand-in: the CC0 MakeHuman hm08 topology (MPFB used as a tool only) reduced to game density with its joint loops, fitted to the approved sculpt reference (landmark warp + surface fit), extra knee, elbow and wrist loops, bare forearms and hands (weapons decision), a grin (parted lips, teeth); separate closed parts (hair and beard shells with chunky clumps, belt, sash with front and back tails, underskirt, 60 rigid skirt plates, ankle and wrist wraps); one 2048 atlas at one texel density; a tangent-space normal map baked from the sculpt (cage, hit-distance mask, normalised blur) plus its cavity and AO and a self-AO of the parts folded into the hand-painted NPR base colour; emissive: bold chest sigil with rays and a white-hot core, a lava crack network over chest, shoulders, forearms and back, the spine crack, the eyes. Polish pass 2026-09-25 (orchestrator review: the blockout column read more like the concept at game size): gauntlets rebuilt on the blockout's own gauntlet, normal/AO bakes, bolder emissive, face and hair/beard. Review sheets in reports/stage2/ (before/after in stage2_polish_before_after.png); honest findings and the acceptance checklist in reports/stage2_production_mesh.md. The remaining human gate is the user's visual approval (item user_visual_approval).

metrics.seed: MakeHuman CC0 game_engine weights, exact per vertex (match p99 0.9 mm), 50/50 with bone heat on torso and limbs, 0 on the hands, 20 % on the head

3_rig.notes: GF_Hero_v1 built from Brax's landmark file (the stage-2 fit's joints, fingers refined on the fitted mesh, weapon sockets exactly at the stage-2 hand frames the anvil_gauntlets were authored in). Weights: MakeHuman CC0 seed + bone heat + twist split + hand-style fixes (knee cap with the thigh, olecranon with the forearm, jaw fold, shoulders, knees); rest-shape prep moves the stage-2 extra loop vertices off their chords (102 verts, <= 8 mm). Parts: hair/beard to head, wraps/belt copy the body, skirt cloth and 60 rigid plates hang from the pelvis and follow the thigh on their side. The identity attach of any weapon GLB on weapon_L/weapon_R is proven in glTF with the exported gauntlets (< 1 um). Honest findings (reports/rig_report.md section 5): front-shoulder crease with the arms forward; knees flatten past ~110 deg (partly stage-2 knee topology); cloth tails need secondary x_ bones (stage 4); the gauntlets are a sleeve weapon: wrist straight, and the elbow cuff presses into the biceps past ~40 deg of elbow flexion (weapon geometry). The user's visual approval is the remaining gate.

user_visual_approval.notes: The user's final visual approval of the AI-made rig and weights (sheets in reports/stage3/, findings in reports/rig_report.md). Record it with approved_by / approved_on on this item.

4_animation.notes: 34 clips on GF_Hero_v1 (24 shared + 10 Brax), keyed in Python Cascadeur-style (effector-driven strong poses: anticipation, contact, follow-through, weight) and solved every frame with an analytic two-bone IK (s4lib.py); in place, 30 fps, loops closed by construction, locomotion speed-matched (playback rate = speed / design speed), planted feet at most 0.9 mm in every clip but the Furnace Rush skid-charge (slide_exempt by design), the anvil_gauntlets wrist rule kept (hand twist only). Naming <key>_<clip>[@loop] (docs/art/GF_HERO_SKELETON.md section 8); events in reports/anim/clips.json (stage 5 writes them to the GLB sidecar). Honest findings (reports/anim_report.md section 6): the gauntlet cuff presses into the biceps in every bent-arm pose (weapon geometry, ~15-25 verts a side), the rigid skirt plates and sash clip the ground and the thighs in lying / kneeling / high-knee poses (no x_ cloth bones yet), deep knee flexion shows the stage-3 knee flattening. The user's visual approval is the remaining gate.

5_export_validate.notes: brax.glb: glTF binary, +Y up, faces +Z, uncompressed (bevy_gltf 0.20 loads no Draco / meshopt / quantisation), GF_Hero_v1 (63 deform joints incl. the 4 sockets) + ONE skinned mesh brax_mesh (the 8 body parts joined: one draw call, single-sided M_brax with 2048 base colour / emissive / normal PNGs, tangents, NO vertex colours - the stage-4 scratch export had shipped the paint masks as COLOR_0/COLOR_1, which Bevy multiplies into the base colour), 34 clips named brax_<clip>[@loop] sampled at 30 fps. Gate: validate_glb.py (stdlib, CI job hero-glb) + the Blender 5.2 re-import (every clip one frame) + source fidelity against the .blend. The sidecar brax.meta.json carries the clip events, weapon-variant swaps, design speeds, sockets and status ai_final_pending_user_approval. The anvil_gauntlets ship as assets/models/weapons/anvil_gauntlets.glb (open + fist variants as separate nodes, left pair under offhand). Re-export is byte-identical. The Bevy-side import test comes with the engine integration.
